after_review: oracle configuration written to the case file; Step 3.5 polish gap; Step 3 closes

s39_C.ess_balancing: EXEMPT for the whole run (balancing_exempt_channels = ['ess']); rho_ess fixed 0.01

s39_D.ess_balancing: TWO-PHASE: exempt (rho_ess fixed 0.01) until the ESS Boyd dual ratio (boyd_ess_dual_ratio = s/eps_dual, which equals dual_ratio_balance at tau = 0) has been < 1 on 5 CONSECUTIVE cycles; from the penalty update of that 5th cycle on, the ESS channel is subject to the standard balancing rule (dead band 5.0, factor 1.5, clamp [1e-4, 1e4]) and the standard freeze rule (10 unchanged with a prior action; absolute 200). The lift is one-way (never re-exempted). The lift cycle and every subsequent ESS action are recorded.
s39_D.launch_condition: after C has exited; never concurrently
s39_D.production_change: a per-channel conditional exemption (default off: no conditional policy, every previous arm and case study unchanged), keyed in penalty_update; the arm sets it by override for 'ess' with threshold 1.0 and 5 consecutive cycles

certification_bar.certified_iff: all three channels (V, PF, ESS) inside their Boyd tolerances (primal ratio <= 1 and dual ratio <= 1) AND every local solve successful, for 10 CONSECUTIVE cycles, within the cap of 300, derived from the trajectory (not the harness stopped_by field)

cost_bar.definition: |Q_arm - Q_run1| <= max objective step over the arm's last 10 cycles + max objective step over run 1's last 10 cycles
cost_bar.gated: NO - Planner interpretation of Addendum 21 (the certification bar is the 10-consecutive test; the rule-nine bar is redefined for reporting). An outside-bar result is flagged in the report lead and blocks nothing automatically; adoption is decided at the review.
cost_bar.reading: inside the bar: the cost difference to run 1 is within stopping slack (indeterminate, consistent with run 1); outside the bar: not explained by stopping slack alone, reported as a difference to be explained - never as a lower-cost or different point (the bar is local and valid only when both runs are settled; the arm is settled under the 10-consecutive bar, run 1 under Addendum 16)

reported_not_gated: per-channel terminal ratio max(primal, dual) for V, PF, ESS
rule-ten objective ratio (terminal objective step / objective tolerance)
V/PF/ESS clamp flags (Planner: retained as a reported validity flag; a clamp is flagged prominently in the report)
cost against run 1 under the new rule-nine bar (below)
certification_bar.run1_status: run 1 remains certified under Addendum 16's rule; it is NOT re-scored under this bar (its longest all-pass streak was 3)
certification_bar.stopping_rule_consequence: the runs use minimum_consecutive_converged_cycles = 10 (override), so the production Boyd stop coincides with the certification bar (production counts consecutive cycles with boyd_all_pass AND local_solves_ok, shared_resources_planning.py ~2735-2741); certification cycle = stop cycle when stopped by Boyd

common_configuration.base: v9 arm A configuration via deep-copied overrides (run 1 config; rho_v 0.0077, rho_pf 0.198 initial; rho_ess 0.01 initial on every network and the ESSO; cold standalone initialization; sigma, S_ref, D5 unchanged)
common_configuration.capture: everything v9 captured, including per-entry PF capture (stride 1, identity asserted per cycle) and the ESS entry stride

decisions_in_force.case_file: data/SRP1/SRP1_params.json is NOT edited by this stage; the adopted oracle configuration is written to the case file only after the stop for review
decisions_in_force.freeze_rule: freeze after 10 unchanged cycles (with >= 1 prior action on that channel) + absolute freeze at cycle 200 (freeze_backstop_cycle = 200)
decisions_in_force.tau: tau = 0 globally is the oracle setting (proximal term removed from the method); per-channel tau is a recorded fallback only on evidence of TSO instability

parallel_work: zero-solve node 7 interface look (P, 2030) at the stop of v9 arms A and B, extended to C and D when available

Step 3.6: replace the per-cycle TSO whole-model clone with a lightweight capture (mutable parameter values + warm-start suffixes; block rebuilt deterministically on demand), in an isolated worktree; integrated, preflighted and gated only after C and D; then 10-cycle re-measurement; then persistent workers
pre_launch_evidence_for_D: before D launches, a zero-solve open-loop replay of the two-phase ESS policy (real _update_admm_penalties) on arm C's completed trajectory (and on v9 arm A's) records the predicted lift cycle and first ESS balancing action; recorded as a note, not a prediction change

predecessor.note: v9 arms A (tau 0) and B (PF balancing) both helped; criterion (c) withdrawn by Addendum 21; v9's s38_C_combined arm (3-consecutive stop) is superseded by s39_C below and is never launched

predictions_recorded_in_advance.adoption: if D certifies with storage terminal ratio < 0.5, D is the production oracle; else C (if C certifies); if neither certifies, stop for review
s39_C: certification (10th consecutive all-pass cycle) by ~145 - operationalized as certification cycle <= 150
s39_D: storage channel terminal ratio max(primal, dual) < 0.5 at certification

report: lead with the certification verdict per arm under the new bar; then certification cycle, first-pass cycles per channel, per-channel terminal ratios, rule ten, cost vs run 1 under the new bar, rho/gamma trajectories with action labels (for D: ESS lift cycle and actions), per-entry PF decomposition, failures, oscillation/TSO-instability monitoring, EFC trajectory, predictions scored, adoption; stop for review after D
stage: P5.15 Addendum 21 - oracle arms C and D under the new certification bar - frozen specification v10
tso_instability_monitoring: v9 trigger definitions (unrecovered case9 failure; case9 failure rate > 2x run 1's 58/477; PF or ESS oscillation flag) evaluated and REPORTED for C and D; no fallback arm is authorized in this stage - evidence of TSO instability is reported for the per-channel-tau decision
